question.problem: A survey of Bulgarian citizens showed that $17%$ of all females and  $38%$ of all males smoke. $51%$ of the population are female. If a smoker from this population is selected at random, what is the probability of them being female? Express your answer as a percentage to the nearest percent.
question.worked_solution:
Let $S$ be the event that a randomly selected person smokes, and let $F$ be the event that they are female. Then, we require $P(F|S),$ which we can compute using Bayes' theorem.

$$
P(F|S)=\frac{P(S|F)P(F)}{P(S)}=\frac{P(S|F)P(F)}{P(S|F)P(F)+P(S|{F}^{′})P({F}^{′})}
$$

From the problem statement, we have the following:

- Since $17%$ of all females and  $38%$ of all males smoke, we have

$$
P(S|F)=0.17,\,P(S|{F}^{′})=0.38.
$$

- Since $51%$ of the population are female, we have

$$
P(F)=0.51,\,P({F}^{′})=1-0.51=0.49.
$$

Therefore, using Bayes' theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(F|S) & =\frac{P(S|F)P(F)}{P(S|F)P(F)+P(S|{F}^{′})P({F}^{′})} \\  & =\frac{(0.17)(0.51)}{(0.17)(0.51)+(0.38)(0.49)} \\  & ≈32%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest percent.
